name: Downtown (Kyauktada & Pabedan)
tagline: Colonial grid between the river and Sule Pagoda
description: Yangon's numbered street grid, holding the largest stock of British-era buildings in Southeast Asia, Bogyoke Aung San Market, Chinatown's night food stalls on 19th Street and the Sule Pagoda roundabout. Apartments are walk-up flats above shophouses. The only genuinely walkable part of the city.
bestFor: Short-stay visitors who want to explore on foot and pay local prices.
pros: Everything reachable on foot, including markets and riverfront
Cheapest rents for a central location
Best street food and teashop culture in Myanmar
cons: Blackouts hit hard, most walk-ups have no generator or lift power
Crumbling buildings, poor drainage and monsoon flooding
Heavy security presence and checkpoints since the 2021 coup

name: Sanchaung
tagline: Young, dense and full of small cafes
description: A tight grid of mid-rise blocks north-west of downtown, long favoured by young professionals and the small foreign crowd who remain. Independent coffee shops, cheap Burmese and Shan restaurants, bars and a busy wet market fill the side streets. Rents sit well below Bahan for a similar location.
bestFor: Anyone who wants cafes, bars and a social scene without Bahan prices.
pros: The most cafe-dense area in Yangon
Good value flats close to the centre
Easy reach of both downtown and the university belt
cons: Rotating power cuts of many hours a day, generator access varies
Congested narrow streets and constant horn noise
Saw significant unrest and raids in past crackdowns

name: Bahan (Golden Valley)
description: The wealthiest township, wrapping around Shwedagon Pagoda and Inya Lake, with leafy Golden Valley lanes of walled colonial villas, embassies, NGO offices and the city's better restaurants and hotels. Almost all remaining diplomats and international staff live here. Generators and backup water are standard.
bestFor: Nomads with budget who need reliable power, backup water and a quiet compound.
pros: Most properties have generators, so blackouts hurt less
Quiet, tree-lined streets and large gardens
Best restaurants, clinics and international services
cons: By far the most expensive rents in Yangon
Isolating, you need a car for everything
Heavy diplomatic and military presence around the pagoda

name: Kamayut (Hledan)
description: The township around Yangon University and the Hledan Junction market, filled with students, cheap canteens, bookstalls, phone repair shops and the Hledan Centre mall. Rents are among the lowest for a well-connected area and Inya Lake sits just north for evening walks.
bestFor: Long-stay budget travellers who want the lowest costs and student energy.
pros: Cheapest rents of the well-connected townships
Very low food costs around the university
Inya Lake and Hledan Centre both close
cons: Long blackouts and unreliable water pressure
Traffic at Hledan Junction is punishing at peak hours
Politically sensitive area, protests and security responses have centred here

name: Yankin
tagline: Quiet condo blocks north-east of the lake
description: A calmer residential township of newer condominium towers, small malls, clinics and international schools, popular with families who want space and a lift that actually works. Streets are wide and low on traffic compared with Sanchaung. Roughly 30 minutes into downtown outside rush hour.
bestFor: Longer stayers who want a modern serviced condo and a quiet street.
pros: Quiet streets, less noise and pollution
Good schools, clinics and supermarkets nearby
cons: Little to walk to, taxis or a car are essential
Almost no cafe or bar scene
Slow, congested commute into the centre
